stemMarkdown: After its price was increased by 12%, an article costs Rs. 1008. What was its price (in Rs.) before the increase?
solutionMarkdown: If the original price is $x$, then $x \times \left(1 + \dfrac{12}{100}\right) = 1008$, so $x = \dfrac{1008 \times 100}{112} = 900$.
altSolutionMarkdown: The new price is 112% of the old, so the old price is $\dfrac{100}{112}$ of Rs. 1008 $=$ Rs. 900.
